C-8.Name: Bind tab cycling to Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab via native Window menu
C-8.Summary: The commands tabs.cycleForward / tabs.cycleBackward exist in the renderer registry but have no accelerator and no menu entry (they sit in the menu-consistency RENDERER_ONLY_ALLOWLIST with the reason "Tab cycling — no standard shortcut"), so the user cannot cycle tabs from the keyboard at all — the primary repro path of the original C-6 bug report. Add "Select Next Tab" (Ctrl+Tab) and "Select Previous Tab" (Ctrl+Shift+Tab) items to the native Window submenu; the existing menu→command bridge dispatches the ids to the already-registered commands (bus mt::tabs-cycle-right/left → editor store).

Problem.Description: No keyboard way to switch tabs; cycling exists only via command palette.
Problem.RootCause: The port never wired v1's cycling accelerators; menu-consistency allowlisted the ids as renderer-only.
Problem.Evidence: grep tabs.cycleForward across src/renderer/src → only commands/index.js definition, descriptions.js, constants.js; no keymap reference. CUA QA 2026-09-16 marked Ctrl+Tab scenarios N/A for exactly this reason.

Goals.R-1: m009_menu.rs Window submenu gains tabs.cycleForward ("Select Next Tab", Ctrl+Tab) and tabs.cycleBackward ("Select Previous Tab", Ctrl+Shift+Tab).
Goals.R-2: menu-consistency test: remove both ids from RENDERER_ONLY_ALLOWLIST and pin the new ids + accelerators against the Rust source.

Constraints.Constraint: Reuse the existing menu-id → renderer-command bridge; no new IPC.
Accelerators use Ctrl (⌃), not Cmd — ⌘Tab is reserved by macOS.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycle tabs in the live app, including past the visible strip edge (strip auto-scrolls per C-6).
menu-consistency suite green with the pins updated.

C-8.VerificationIntent: tests/renderer/commands/menu-consistency.test.js pins; CUA live check: cycle with Ctrl+Tab past the strip edge and watch the active tab stay visible.

Approval.ApprovalScope: Implement with the C-7/C-9 batch; same review + CUA gates.
